- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model consistently overpredicts after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean is often too high in early horizon (e.g., 1–7 days ahead); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5 depending on sentiment volatility.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a downward correction starting at day 8–10.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates by 1–3% in high-sentiment periods; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if sentiment > 0.7.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.2–0.4), model tends to drift upward; apply a 0.3–0.7% downward correction to prevent overshoot.
